### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. anauxetic dysplasia 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.775)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:10031)

**Proposed mechanism:** RMRP (HGNC:10031) —DISRUPTS→ RNase MRP RNA processing (GO:0006425); RNase MRP RNA processing (GO:0006425) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0002650); RNase MRP RNA processing (GO:0006425) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004304). Mutations in RMRP disrupt RNase MRP RNA processing, leading to downstream skeletal dysplasia and short stature phenotypes observed in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct causal genes for each disease or demonstration that mutations in RMRP lead to gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects rather than loss-of-function. _(variant: rs749175069 (a known pathogenic variant in RMRP))_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism in RMRP allows for potential therapeutic strategies targeting RNA processing or downstream pathways common to both skeletal dysplasia and short stature.

#### 2. cartilage-hair hypoplasia  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.770)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:10031)

**Proposed mechanism:** RMRP (HGNC:10031) —DISRUPTS→ Ribonucleoprotein complex biogenesis (GO:0000326); Ribonucleoprotein complex biogenesis (GO:0000326) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0004325); Ribonucleoprotein complex biogenesis (GO:0000326) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal hair morphology (HP:0001076); Ribonucleoprotein complex biogenesis (GO:0000326) —LEADS_TO→ Aniridia (HP:0000497). Loss-of-function mutations in RMRP disrupt ribonucleoprotein complex biogenesis, leading to a shared downstream effect that manifests as skeletal dysplasia (common to both CHH and aniridia), abnormal hair morphology (characteristic of CHH), and aniridia (characteristic of aniridia).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in RMRP that are exclusively associated with either aniridia or cartilage-hair hypoplasia, but not overlapping, would challenge this shared mechanism. Alternatively, if specific variants in RMRP were shown to have divergent functional consequences (e.g., LoF for one disease and GoF for the other) this would falsify the shared mechanism.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of RMRP in these distinct rare diseases could facilitate the identification of common therapeutic targets or strategies for conditions affecting skeletal development and other complex phenotypes.
